Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph CILG OPINION NO JAN 3 1 2025 MR. MENANDRAO MACALINAO macalinaomenandrao@gmail.com Dear Mr. Macalinao: This has reference to an electronic email ("e-mail") you sent dated 5 June 2024, seeking this Department's legal opinion concerning the propriety of working from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM as an appointive official (barangay administrator) of the barangay while serving simultaneously as a private school teacher. Specifically, you have raised the following issue, which we quoted in verbatim: "Paano niya gagampanan ang isa trabaho ng isang administrador kung sya ay nag tuturo sa pribadong paaralaan? Sa madaling salita hindi niya nagagampanan ng mabuti ang kanyang tungkulin sa gobyerno na dapat ay 8:00 ng umaga hanggang 5:00 ng hapon dahil sya ay naalis sa barangay?" Settled is the rule that barangay appointive and elective officials are not forbidden to practice their profession provided that they secure prior permission or authorization from the head of their Department, as required by civil service regulation. Section 12, Rule XVIII of the Revised Civil Service Rules is applicable, to wit: Section 12. No officer or employee shall engage directly in any private business, vocation, or profession or be connected with any commercial, credit, agricultural, or industrial undertaking without a written permission from the head of Department; Provided, That this prohibition will be absolute in the case of those officers and employees whose duties and responsibilities require that their entire time be at the disposal of the Government: Provided, further, That if an employee is granted permission to engage in outside activities, the time so devoted outside of office hours should be fixed by the chief of the agency to the end that it will not impair in any way the efficiency of the other officer or employee: And provided, finally, That no permission is necessary in the case of investments, made by an officer or employee, which do not involve any real or apparent conflict between his private interests and public duties, or in any way influence him in the discharge of his duties, and he shall not take part in the management of the enterprise or become an officer or member of the board of directors.' Be that as it may, while appointive barangay officials are allowed to practice their profession, however, being public officials, Republic Act No. 6713, otherwise known as the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees" shall apply. Section 7 (b) (2) thereof provides that public officials and employees, like barangay officials, may practice their profession provided that such practice will not conflict with their officials functions, viz: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

"Section 7. Prohibited Acts and Transactions. — xxx xxx (b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto. — Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: (2) Engage in private practice of their profession unless authorized by the Constitution or law, provided, that such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict with their official functions• od' xxx Relatedly, Section 136 of the 2017 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Action which states that: "No officer or employee, whether in a permanent or regular capacity, temporary, casual, or hold-over, shall engage directly or indirectly in any private business or practice of profession. Exemptions may be allowed subject to the limitations provided under R.A. No. 6713 and other special laws. Provided, further, that the following requirements/conditions are met: a. Written permission from the head of agency must be secured and renewed annually; b. Time devoted outside of office hours shall not in any way impair the efficiency of the officer or employee nor pose conflict or tend to conflict with the official functions and must be fixed by the head of the agency; and c. Government facilities, equipment and supplies shall not be used while engaged in private business or practice of profession. In view thereof, it is incumbent upon the Barangay Administrator to comply with the above-mentioned conditions in order to validly engage in the private practice of his/her profession. Among the above-enumerated requirements, we put particular emphasis on Item B, that your services as a private school teacher should be rendered outside the official working hours required of you as a barangay administrator. This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts presented and our appreciation of the same without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of other government agencies and the courts. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jvpr Page 2 of 2
